claim: Taquería Frontera in Cypress Park tops L.A. TACO's al pastor list with Tijuana-imported tortillas, trompo-seared al pastor, cilantro crema, and grilled pineapple.
quote: Frontera's al pastor taco... yellow tortillas imported from El Grano de Oro tortilleria in Tijuana... al pastor slow-cooked and seared on the trompo, and finished with a custom salsa, cilantro crema, and a slice of lightly grilled pineapple.

claim: The Infatuation ranks LA's 25 best tacos, with Leo's Tacos al pastor carved fresh from the trompo and Tacos El Gordo serving Tijuana-style carne asada among the staples.
quote: The 25 Best Tacos In Los Angeles, Ranked

claim: Standout Grand Central Market stalls include Villa's Tacos (blue-corn quesatacos), Broad Street Oyster's $25 lobster rolls, For The Win smashburgers, and Maple Block Texas brisket.
quote: Villa's Tacos GCM... quesatacos with Dodger-blue corn tortillas and razor-thin cheese crusts that crackle... Broad Street Oyster GCM... $25 warm lobster rolls with drawn butter

claim: Langer's #19 pastrami (open at Alvarado and 7th since 1947) is touted as the best in America, and Philippe the Original (1908) claims to have invented the French dip.
quote: Fans of the Original #19 at Langer's... tout it as the best in America... Langer's is at the same location on the corner of Alvarado and 7th since it opened in 1947... Philippe the Original was opened by Philippe Mathieu in 1908

claim: The Infatuation's LA coffee picks span Silver Lake's Picnic, Highland Park's Comet Over Delphi, and a two-story Yemeni cafe Qamaria in Culver City.
quote: The 14 Best Coffee Shops In LA

claim: LA's local coffee shops carve identities by roasting their own beans and drawing on cultural backgrounds, e.g. Picaresca's cafe de olla latte and Mexican mocha.
quote: As a Latinx-owned coffee shop, Picaresca's signature drinks are drawn from traditional Mexican drinks, like the cafe de olla latte, Mexican mocha, and tamarind espresso tonic.

claim: Park's BBQ is the most-named best Korean BBQ in LA, holds a spot in the MICHELIN Guide, and serves USDA Prime and Kobe-style beef in Koreatown.
quote: Park's BBQ is the restaurant that most critics and locals name first... It holds a coveted spot in the MICHELIN Guide and serves USDA Prime and Kobe-style beef.

claim: Time Out's April 2026 Koreatown KBBQ guide names Baekjeong, Pigya (pork-focused), and Ahgassi Gopchang (open until 1am weekends) among top spots.
quote: Ahgassi Gopchang is a massive spot on 6th Street... a room filled with smoky tabletop grills and clanking soju glasses that goes off until 1am on weekends... Pigya in Koreatown is big on pork.

claim: The San Gabriel Valley is the densest concentration of Asian dining in the US, with Sichuan standouts like Chengdu Taste (Michelin-recognized) and Mian's dan dan noodles.
quote: The Best Restaurants In The San Gabriel Valley

claim: SGV Sichuan picks include Chengdu Taste in Alhambra (boiled fish, dan dan noodles), MIAN, and sleeper hit Xiang La Hui (Chongqing fried chicken, toothpick lamb).
quote: Chengdu Taste at 828 W Valley Blvd in Alhambra is a Michelin-recognized Sichuan restaurant known for boiled fish and dan dan noodles... Xiang La Hui is a sleeper Sichuan hit of the SGV with top-notch Chongqing fried chicken

claim: LA rooftop bars include Inanna (poolside Mediterranean atop DTLA's Hoxton), Florentin (8th-floor hidden DTLA lounge), and Osa (San Gabriel Mountain views in Pasadena).
quote: Inanna Bar - A poolside Mediterranean spot on top of DTLA's The Hoxton... Florentin - A semi-hidden DTLA rooftop... Osa - Located on top of the AC Hotel Pasadena... views of the San Gabriel Mountains

claim: The Infatuation maintains a guide to LA's 17 best cocktail bars covering the broader craft-cocktail scene beyond rooftops.
quote: The 17 Best Cocktail Bars In Los Angeles
